# 44 CFR Part 61 Appendix A(1) - Standard Flood Insurance Policy Dwelling Form

## I. Agreement

We will pay you for direct physical loss by or from flood to your insured property
if you have paid the full amount due, complied with all terms and conditions of
this policy, and furnished accurate information and statements.

## II. Definitions

### Flood

Flood means a general and temporary condition of partial or complete inundation
of two or more acres of normally dry land area or of two or more properties,
one of which is your property, from overflow of inland or tidal waters.

Flood also includes unusual and rapid accumulation or runoff of surface waters
from any source, mudflow, and collapse or subsidence along the shore of a lake
or similar body of water as a result of erosion caused by waves or currents of
water exceeding anticipated cyclical levels.

### Direct Physical Loss By Or From Flood

Direct physical loss by or from flood means loss or damage to insured property
that is directly caused by a flood. There must be evidence of physical changes
to the property.

## V. Exclusions

### Water Or Water-Borne Material

We do not insure for loss to property caused directly by earth movement even if
the earth movement is caused by flood.

Water, moisture, mildew, or mold damage that results primarily from any
condition substantially confined to the dwelling or that is within your control,
including but not limited to design, structural, or mechanical defects; failure,
stoppage, or breakage of water or sewer lines, drains, pumps, fixtures, or
equipment; or failure to inspect and maintain the property after a flood recedes
is excluded.

We do not pay for a loss caused by water, moisture, mildew, or mold damage from
a sewer backup unless there is a flood in the area and the flood is the
proximate cause of the sewer backup.

## VII. General Conditions

### Requirements In Case Of Loss

In case of a flood loss to insured property, you must give prompt written notice
to us.

As soon as reasonably possible, separate the damaged and undamaged property,
putting it in the best possible order so that we may examine it.

Prepare an inventory of damaged property showing the quantity, description,
actual cash value, and amount of loss. Attach all bills, receipts, and related
documents.

Within 60 days after the loss, send us a proof of loss, which is your statement
of the amount you are claiming under the policy signed and sworn to by you.

The proof of loss must furnish the date and time of loss, a brief explanation
of how the loss happened, details about ownership and other insurance, changes
in title or occupancy, names of mortgagees or lienholders, and specifications
of damaged buildings and detailed repair estimates.
